paper.title: StreamGrid: Streaming Point Cloud Analytics via Compulsory Splitting and Deterministic Termination

reading.scope: Physical pages 2–12: splitting, deterministic termination, co-training, buffer modeling, evaluation and limitations. Page 1 retains prior abstract reading; pages 13–14 are not declared read.

findings: Compulsory splitting and early termination change search work and task quality. They are not semantics-preserving GPU compiler transformations.
Buffer ILP holds throughput fixed and needs an explicitly supplied dataflow, timing and reuse model; slowing faster stages can reduce buffering without slowing the bottleneck.
PointNet++ co-training, segmentation and 3DGS use different subsets/quality conditions. CPU-emulated training overhead and accelerator inference savings are separate.

RTL synthesis/layout and cycle/bandwidth modeling are not a deployed current GPU serving framework. Equal-throughput buffer comparisons and comparisons to different specialized accelerators answer different questions.
Figure 20(b) caption and plotted task metric differ in the archived v1; no performance percentage or task-quality generalization is adopted.
paper_to_framework_gap: No current inference-framework integration verified. Changes in algorithmic work, training adaptation and modeled hardware prevent treating the reported speedup as an interchangeable kernel optimization.
scope: Declared paper sections and visual pages only. Existing chapter resource/quality reasoning is sufficient; no new main section, case, lab or figure, no hardware or downloaded-code execution.
